data.title: Red Robin Shares Down on Wider Loss, Lower Revenue
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Red Robin Gourmet Burgers shares tumbled after the company logged a wider loss and lower revenue, missing Wall Street expectations.

Shares fell 16% to $6.70 in after-hours trading on Wednesday. The stock was down 2.6% at $7.95 through market-close, and is up 96% year to date.

The burger chain posted a third-quarter loss of $21.2 million, or $1.12 a share, compared with a loss of $18.4 million, or $1.03, the year earlier.

Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings per share came in at a loss of 54 cents. Analysts polled by Factset expected a loss of 34 cents.

Revenue declined to $232.1 million from $265.1 million, below the $253.6 Wall Street analysts were expecting. However, comparable restaurant sales increased 3.9%, driven by a 5.6% increase in average guest check that benefited from one year anniversary of its Big Yummm value platform.

In the third quarter, the company advanced its restructuring plan by refranchising restaurants, using the proceeds to reduce debt and then refinancing debt at improved terms, Chief Executive Dave Pace said. Red Robin had refranchised 108 company-owned restaurants for a total cash consideration of about $89.4 million.

Red Robin expects fourth-quarter comparable restaurant revenue growth of about 2.75%, up from its previous 0.5% to 1.5% guidance.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: Weil Gotshal Bankruptcy Team Heading to Skadden — WSJ
data.description:
By Erin Mulvaney

The leader of Weil, Gotshal & Manges's bankruptcy practice, which was once the law firm's crown jewel, will join rival Skadden Arps.

Skadden is set to announce Wednesday that it hired about 40 bankruptcy lawyers, including 11 partners, from Weil — a firm that helped shepherd some of the country's most high-profile bankruptcies and is now itself dissolving.

Matt Barr, who led Weil's bankruptcy practice and was also an influential voice on its management committee, will now head Skadden's restructuring group. The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Barr was in talks with Skadden. He will stay at Weil through the end of the year.

Several other firms were actively recruiting Barr and his team, including Cleary Gottlieb and Paul Weiss, the Journal previously reported.

Weil invented much of modern bankruptcy practice and spent years as a go-to adviser for corporations under duress. It has handled many of the country's largest and most complex restructuring matters, including Lehman Brothers, General Motors, and Washington Mutual.

Weil's leading position in the bankruptcy world was overtaken by larger competitors, and some of its best talent had been picked off. The firm overall had experienced stagnant growth in recent years, which was part of the reason that it started to crater as more partners eyed the exits. Many in the industry saw a bitter irony in the firm that had helped guide some of the country's largest corporations through bankruptcy now having to engineer its own demise.

Skadden historically had a strong bankruptcy practice, including handling matters for American Airlines, MGM, and Charter Communications, but it has lost ground to rivals in recent years.

Weil's decision to wind down last month left hundreds of lawyers looking for new roles. Since the wind down was announced, other firms including Simpson Thacher, Kirkland & Ellis Gibson Dunn, Paul Weiss and Cleary Gottlieb have also scooped up the firm's talent.

Barr was elevated to head of Weil's restructuring group in July. He is known for his work representing First Brands Group in its complex bankruptcy, as well as on major energy-related chapter 11 proceedings such as EP Energy, Talen Energy and Fieldwood Energy. He also handled the bankruptcy of CEC Entertainment, the parent company of Chuck E. Cheese.

data.title: What the 'death cross' in small-cap stocks means for the rest of the stock market
data.description:
By Tomi Kilgore

The negative chart pattern confirms weakness in the Russell 2000 and in overall market breadth, says Oppenheimer's top chart watcher

A bearish "death cross" pattern has appeared in the chart of the Russell 2000 small-cap index, warning that stocks still have room to fall.

The technical outlook for the Russell 2000 has gone from bad to worse over the past month, as the small-cap stock index has crossed another negative threshold that warns the rest of the market is at risk of further weakness.

Small-cap stocks can be more sensitive to market stress - particularly the kind that Wall Street has been dealing with in recent months - than their larger counterparts. Smaller companies can be hurt more by rising interest rates than bigger, more established companies, because they tend to be more reliant on borrowing and floating-rate debt. And large-cap companies are likely to have more options than their smaller counterparts to find ways to deal with tariffs and higher fuel costs.

When the Russell 2000 RUT entered correction territory on Oct. 14 - defined as a decline of at least 10% from a recent peak - two months after it had closed at a record high, the S&P 500 SPX was just 1.3% below its own record high reached just six sessions earlier.

Ari Wald, head of technical analysis at Oppenheimer & Co., was not surprised. He noted that small caps tend to peak before large caps - though, on the bright side, they also often bottom first. "As go small caps, so goes the market cycle," Wald said in a phone interview with MarketWatch.

On Wednesday, for the first time in 20 months, the Russell 2000's 50-day moving average, viewed as a shorter-term trend tracker, crossed below its 200-day moving average, which is seen by many as a border between longer-term uptrends and downtrends. This technical event, known as a "death cross," is viewed as marking the spot where the index's decline has gone far enough, and lasted long enough, to earn the title of a longer-term downtrend.

Keep in mind that moving-average crossovers aren't necessarily meant to be good market-timing tools. They are like diplomas - acknowledgments of the work put in to get the index to where it is. As Wald likes to say, all major downside moves start with a death cross, but not all death crosses lead to a major decline. But that doesn't mean they have no predictive value.

"The death cross is confirmation of the weakness we've seen in the Russell 2000, and market breadth overall," Wald said. Basically, what started out as a selloff in Big Tech and artificial-intelligence-related stocks has since spread to other areas of the market.

The Russell 2000's last death cross appeared on March 20, 2025, which was before President Trump's "liberation day" tariff announcement triggered a brief market panic. After the death cross, the Russell 2000 fell another 15% in a little over two weeks before bottoming.

The S&P 500 followed with a death cross of its own, but not until April 14, which was four sessions after that index had bottomed.

There were two death-cross appearance in the Russell 2000 chart in 2023. The first was on April 21 and the second appeared on Oct. 13; the index fell another 4.1% and 4.8%, respectively, before it bottomed. The S&P 500 did not see a death cross that year.

Before that, a death cross popped up for the Russell 2000 on Jan. 19, 2022, 37 trading sessions before one appeared on the S&P 500's chart. The Russell 2000 sank a further 20% before it hit bottom five months later.

While these previous death-cross appearances hardly make a case for what investors should expect going forward - or whether the S&P 500 will eventually follow with its own death cross - they do send an ominous message.

"We're moving in the wrong direction, and we've crossed another threshold," Wald said.

The Russell 2000 rose 0.5% on Wednesday, after closing Tuesday at a seven-month low 11.9% below its Aug. 14 peak. In comparison, the S&P 500 closed Wednesday at a five-month low, 6.3% below its Oct. 6 record high. At current trajectories, it could take more than a month before the S&P 500's 50-DMA crosses below its 200-DMA.

As painful as the recent selloff has been, Wald believes there's still more to come. "I don't think we're at that extreme yet, to be at a bottom," he said.

-Tomi Kilgore

data.title: TIME Names Bloom Energy Among America’s Top Manufacturers of 2027
data.description:
Bloom Energy (), a global leader in power solutions, today announced that it has been named to TIME's list of America's Top Manufacturers of 2027.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118727682/en/

America's Top Manufacturers of 2027

The list, developed by TIME and Statista, recognizes 250 U.S. manufacturers based on financial performance, innovation capacity and employment metrics. Companies were evaluated using measures including revenue growth, research and development investment, workforce growth and retention, and workplace safety.

“At Bloom, technology and manufacturing innovation go hand in hand,” said Satish Chitoori, Chief Operations Officer at Bloom Energy. “We have spent years building the people, processes and manufacturing capability required to take a highly complex energy technology and produce it at scale in the United States. That capability matters more than ever as demand for power is growing at a pace the traditional infrastructure model was not designed to meet. The digital era requires digital power solutions, and Bloom meets that need for a wide range of essential industries. This recognition belongs to the teams who make that possible every day.”

Bloom manufactures its fuel cell technology in the United States, with manufacturing operations in Fremont, California, and Newark, Delaware. The company’s platform provides clean, highly reliable power that can be rapidly deployed onsite, helping customers meet growing electricity requirements as power demand accelerates across data centers, commercial and industrial sectors, and other critical industries.

TIME's recognition comes as U.S. manufacturing is increasingly important to the infrastructure required to support AI and data center growth. In announcing the 2027 list, TIME highlighted electrical equipment as the sector with the largest representation among America's top manufacturers and pointed to surging demand associated with data center construction.

TIME and Statista considered thousands of companies with at least $100 million in 2025 revenue and U.S. production facilities. The analysis drew on company disclosures, public databases, patent analytics, Form 10-K filings, ESG and CSR reports, and Occupational Safety and Health Administration data.

The full TIME list and methodology are available here.

About Bloom Energy

Bloom Energy empowers enterprises to meet soaring energy demands and responsibly take charge of their power needs. The company’s fuel cell systems provide ultra-reliable, clean and highly scalable onsite electricity for Fortune 500 customers around the world, including data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, large utilities and other commercial and industrial sectors, as well as mission-critical organizations in local communities, such as hospitals, college campuses and retailers. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, Bloom Energy employs more than 2,000 people worldwide and manufactures its systems in the United States. For more information, visit BloomEnergy.com.

data.title: Livsayis™ (cemdisiran) Approved by the FDA as First and Only siRNA Therapy in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis and Only Treatment with Four-Times-a-Year Subcutaneous Dosing
data.description:
Approval based on Phase 3 NIMBLE results demonstrating rapid, deep and sustained disease control that is maintained throughout three-month dosing intervals

Livsayis is Regeneron's first approved siRNA therapy and neurology medicine

TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Livsayis™ (cemdisiran) for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive, the predominant form of the disease. Livsayis is a novel, complement component factor 5 (C5)-directed small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic that reduces levels of circulating C5 protein, limiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of the disease. It is the first and only approved siRNA therapy in gMG and the only FDA-approved gMG treatment administered subcutaneously four times a year.

“For people living with gMG, every day can be unpredictable, due to fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigue. They may also experience severe exacerbations that can be life-threatening. Many still experience suboptimal disease control, whether from waning of therapeutic effect, inadequate response or high treatment burden,” said Tuan Vu, M.D., Professor of Neurology at the University of South Florida Morsani College of Medicine, Division Director for Neuromuscular Medicine and EMG Laboratories, and a global principal investigator of the NIMBLE trial. “In the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial, Livsayis delivered rapid, deep disease control – maintained through the end of dosing intervals – and offers a four-times-a-year subcutaneous dosing schedule. These results highlight how a first-of-its-kind approach can address a key driver of disease and provide a compelling treatment option.”

The FDA approval was based on results from the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial. Livsayis demonstrated the following least square mean change from baseline:

  • 4.5-point improvement on the Myasthenia Gravis-Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) total score at 24 weeks (0.4 standard error [SE]) compared to a 2.2-point improvement with placebo (0.5 SE). This corresponded to a placebo-adjusted improvement of 2.3 points (p=0.0005). MG-ADL is a clinician-administered patient-reported assessment of daily functions impacted by gMG, such as talking, chewing, swallowing, breathing, vision and mobility. The proportion of MG-ADL responders with at least 3-point improvement at week 24 was greater for Livsayis (76.6%) compared to placebo (44.1%, p<0.001).
  • 4.2-point improvement in Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) total score at 24 weeks (0.6 SE) compared to a 1.5-point improvement with placebo (0.7 SE), corresponding to a placebo-adjusted improvement of 2.8 points (p=0.0015). QMG is a clinician-administered assessment of muscle function, including vision, speaking/swallowing, breathing and limb mobility. The proportion of QMG responders with at least a 5-point improvement at week 24 was greater for Livsayis (48.4%) compared to placebo (19.0%, p<0.001).
  • Rapid onset of clinically meaningful benefit in MG-ADL (2.5 points), with improvements seen as early as two weeks of starting treatment that deepened over time.
  • Sustained disease control and symptom relief through 24 weeks, with MG-ADL scores maintained and no indication of waning efficacy.

The prescribing information for Livsayis includes a Boxed Warning for serious meningococcal infections in addition to warnings and precautions for other serious infections, consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity. The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) in patients treated with Livsayis and more frequently than placebo were injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections. Livsayis is available only through a restricted program called the Livsayis Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS), which is also consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity. Details of the Important Safety Information are included below.

“Livsayis is Regeneron’s first approved medicine in neurology, and an important new option for people living with generalized myasthenia gravis who need effective disease control without a heavy treatment burden,” said George D. Yancopoulos, M.D., Ph.D., Board Co-Chair, President and Chief Scientific Officer of Regeneron. “As Regeneron’s first approved siRNA therapy, this approval marks a meaningful step forward for our neuroscience pipeline as we relentlessly pursue bold, new approaches to transform care for people living with serious neurological diseases.”

“Individuals living with gMG experience profound muscle weakness that can affect how they talk, see, breathe and move, and with it their ability to carry out everyday activities,” said Samantha Masterson, President & CEO, Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America. “This approval is a positive milestone for the gMG community, reflecting continued progress on outcomes that matter most to patients. With Livsayis, those living with generalized myasthenia gravis have a new option that may help maintain disease control while reducing the burden treatment can place on daily life.”

Regeneron is committed to supporting people living with rare diseases and ensuring patients who have been prescribed Livsayis access to their medication. Regeneron’s myRARE™ program offers resources to help patients and healthcare providers, including product information, insurance benefit verification, and information about potential financial support. To learn about myRARE, visit myRARE.com or call 1-833-4my-RARE (1-833-469-7273).

A regulatory submission for Livsayis for the treatment of gMG is currently under review in the European Union, with a decision anticipated in the second half of 2027. Regulatory submissions are planned in additional markets, including Japan.

About gMG

gMG is a rare, chronic autoimmune disease characterized by unpredictable, debilitating and potentially life-threatening muscle weakness. In the most common form of the disease, abnormal anti-AChR antibodies activate the complement system including C5, disrupting communication between nerves and muscles, which contributes to damage at the neuromuscular junction. For these patients, the disease affects muscles throughout the body, resulting in extreme fatigue and difficulties with facial expression, speech, swallowing, mobility, breathing as well as severe exacerbations, including myasthenic crisis that can impair breathing to the point of requiring hospitalization. Worldwide, an estimated 150 to 200 out of every million people have MG. In the U.S., the disease impacts approximately 85,000 people.

About Livsayis

Livsayis is the first approved siRNA therapy for gMG and the only gMG treatment FDA-approved to be administered subcutaneously four times per year (every three months).

Livsayis is a complement C5-directed siRNA that degrades the messenger RNA (mRNA) that encodes the C5 protein, thereby blocking C5 production, reducing circulating levels of C5 and inhibiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of AChR-positive gMG.

Regeneron is solely responsible for the development, manufacturing, and commercialization of Livsayis through a worldwide licensing agreement with Alnylam.

About the NIMBLE trial

NIMBLE is the largest global, interventional gMG trial conducted to date. In this ongoing Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, Livsayis is being evaluated in patients with anti-AChR antibody-positive gMG who can continue background immunosuppressants based on the investigator’s discretion. Participants were randomized to receive one of four subcutaneous regimens: Livsayis every three months; a combination of Livsayis and a C5-inhibiting monoclonal antibody every 4 weeks; C5-inhibiting monoclonal antibody every 4 weeks; or placebo every 4 weeks.

The primary endpoint assessed changes in the MG-ADL total score from baseline to week 24. The MG-ADL scale is an eight-question clinician-administered, patient-reported tool that measures how gMG affects aspects of daily life and provides a total score ranging from 0 to 24. The key secondary endpoint was the change from baseline in QMG total score at week 24. The QMG is a clinician-administered 13-item standardized assessment evaluating muscle function that provides a total score ranging from 0 to 39. In both MG-ADL and QMG, a higher total score indicates greater disease severity, and a larger reduction in total score indicates greater improvement in disease symptoms and better treatment effect.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about LIVSAYIS?

LIVSAYIS is a medicine that affects part of your immune system. LIVSAYIS may lower the ability of your immune system to fight certain infections.

  • LIVSAYIS increases your chance of getting serious meningococcal infections caused by Neisseria meningitidis bacteria. Meningococcal infections may quickly become life-threatening or cause death if not recognized and treated early.
    • You must complete your meningococcal vaccines at least 2 weeks before your first dose of LIVSAYIS.
    • If you have not completed your meningococcal vaccines, and LIVSAYIS must be started right away, you should receive the required vaccines as soon as possible.
    • If you have not been vaccinated and LIVSAYIS must be started right away, you must also receive antibiotics.
    • If you had a meningococcal vaccine in the past, you might need additional vaccination before starting LIVSAYIS. Your healthcare provider will decide if you need additional meningococcal vaccination.
    • Meningococcal vaccines do not prevent all meningococcal infections. Call your healthcare provider or get emergency medical help right away if you get any of these signs and symptoms of a meningococcal infection: fever, fever and a rash, fever with high heart rate, headache with nausea or vomiting, headache and a fever, headache with a stiff neck or stiff back, confusion, muscle aches with flu-like symptoms, or eyes sensitive to light

Your healthcare provider will give you a Patient Safety Card about the risk of serious meningococcal infection. Carry it with you at all times during treatment and for 12 months after your last LIVSAYIS dose. Your risk of meningococcal infection may continue for several months after your last dose of LIVSAYIS. It is important to show this card to any healthcare provider who treats you. This will help them diagnose and treat you quickly.

LIVSAYIS is only available through a program called the LIVSAYIS Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). Before you can receive LIVSAYIS, your healthcare provider must: enroll in the LIVSAYIS REMS program; counsel you about the risk of serious meningococcal infections; give you the Patient Guide that explains your risk of serious meningococcal infections; give you a Patient Safety Card that has important information about the signs and symptoms of meningococcal infections; make sure that you are vaccinated against serious infections caused by meningococcal bacteria, and that you receive antibiotics if you need to start LIVSAYIS right away and you are not up-to-date on your vaccines.

LIVSAYIS may also increase the risk of other types of serious infections especially those caused by encapsulated bacteria, including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Certain people may be at risk of serious infections with gonorrhea. Talk to your healthcare provider about whether you are at risk for gonorrhea infection, about gonorrhea prevention, and regular testing.

Call your healthcare provider right away if you have new signs or symptoms of infection.

Who should not receive LIVSAYIS?

  • Do not receive LIVSAYIS if you have a serious meningococcal infection when you are starting LIVSAYIS treatment.

Before you receive LIVSAYIS, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions, including if you:

  • Have an infection or fever
  • Are pregnant or plan to be pregnant. It is not known whether LIVSAYIS will harm your unborn baby
  • Are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if LIVSAYIS passes into your breast milk

Tell your healthcare provider about medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Know the medicines you take and the vaccines you receive. Keep a list of them to show your healthcare provider and pharmacist when you get a new medicine.

The most common side effects in people with gMG treated with LIVSAYIS include: injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections.

Tell your healthcare provider about any side effect that bothers you or that does not go away. These are not all the possible side effects of LIVSAYIS. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Please see full Prescribing Information, including Boxed WARNING, and Medication Guide for LIVSAYIS.

What is LIVSAYIS?

LIVSAYIS is a prescription medicine used to treat a disease called generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adults who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive.

It is not known if LIVSAYIS is safe and effective in children.

About Regeneron

Regeneron is a leading biotechnology company that invents, develops and commercializes life-transforming medicines for people with serious diseases. Founded and led by physician-scientists, our unique ability to repeatedly and consistently translate science into medicine has led to numerous approved treatments and product candidates in development, most of which were homegrown in our laboratories. Our medicines and pipeline are designed to help patients with eye diseases, allergic and inflammatory diseases, cancer, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurological diseases, hematologic conditions, infectious diseases, and rare diseases.

Regeneron pushes the boundaries of scientific discovery and accelerates drug development using our proprietary technologies, such as VelociSuite®, which produces optimized fully human antibodies and new classes of bispecific antibodies. We are shaping the next frontier of medicine with data-powered insights from the Regeneron Genetics Center® and pioneering genetic medicine platforms, enabling us to identify innovative targets and complementary approaches to potentially treat or cure diseases.

For more information, please visit www.Regeneron.com or follow Regeneron on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook or X.

data.title: Sanford Bull Sees Strong Cash Generation in FY27 — Market Talk
data.description: Sanford's bull at Forsyth Barr shrugs off the prospect of lower profitability in FY27. That's because the New Zealand company had an exceptional squid season a year earlier, which will make it hard for FY27 wildcatch earnings to beat FY26. Analyst Paul Laxton Koraua also points to an unwinding of salmon biomass valuation gains in FY27 and further pressure on Sanford's mussels division. "However, cash generation should remain strong, supporting our forecast for a broadly net cash position by the end of FY27," Forsyth Barr says. It retains an "outperform" call on Sanford, noting its one-year forward price-to-earnings multiple of 11x represents an around 34% discount to the market median. Sanford is unchanged, at NZ$7.00, today. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)

data.title: UniCredit and Germany reach broad agreement on Commerzbank takeover
data.description:
By Holger Hansen

UniCredit and Germany have reached agreement on the big sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, a major development in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

The agreement, laid out in a letter from UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil as well as a separate statement to Reuters from the German minister, states that the merged bank's German headquarters will remain in Frankfurt as a listed entity, a key German demand.

But Germany has given up its insistence on naming two supervisory board members to Commerzbank , in a concession to UniCredit.

A combination of UniCredit and Commerzbank would create a bank with more than €1.3 trillion ($1.43 trillion) in assets across two of the euro zone's ​largest economies in one of the most significant cross-border European banking deals in years.

In the letter dated November 18 and seen by Reuters, Orcel said he was "prepared to commit" to a series of binding principles and thanked Klingbeil for discussions "which have allowed us to find common ground."

UniCredit also pledged to put German nationals on UniCredit's board of directors.

Klingbeil, in his statement to Reuters, said Germany "supports a swift process and an orderly transition of control."

"We have reached common ground and UniCredit has made clear commitments to Germany as a business location, to the rights of Commerzbank employees and to a continued constructive dialogue with the works council in the further process," Klingbeil said, referring to a body of elected employee representatives.

Orcel pounced on Commerzbank in 2024, taking the lender and the government off guard by discreetly building up a holding. Commerzbank and Berlin tried to prevent the ⁠takeover, ​but gave in after UniCredit amassed a stake nearing ​50%.

The German government holds a 13.3% stake in Commerzbank following a bailout during the global financial crisis.

($1 = 0.9115 euros)

data.title: Hy-Vee Health with Oscar Expands Across Iowa, Into Kansas City and Omaha for 2027 Open Enrollment
data.description:
Hy-Vee, Inc. ("Hy-Vee"), a leading grocery store in the Midwest, and Oscar, one of the fastest-growing insurers in the individual market and part of Oscar Health (), today announced that Hy-Vee Health with Oscar is expanding statewide across Iowa and launching in Kansas City and Omaha for 2027 Open Enrollment.1

Beginning Nov. 1, 2026, individuals and families can enroll in Hy-Vee Health with Oscar directly through HealthCare.gov for 2027 coverage. Employees in CHOICE Arrangements (formerly ICHRA) can also enroll using their tax-free monthly employer contributions.

Hy-Vee became joint owner of Exemplar Care in 2024, rebranding the direct primary care practice as Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care and helping the practice expand to more than 17 clinic locations across the Midwest.

The Hy-Vee Health with Oscar plan makes getting care as easy as shopping at Hy-Vee. Members get a full suite of healthcare, lifestyle, and shopping benefits in one comprehensive package:

  • Budget-friendly coverage and medications: Competitive monthly premiums and affordable prescriptions available at Hy-Vee pharmacies for individuals and the whole family.

  • Free care at Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care2 (a $2,600 value for a family of four3): $0 primary care, urgent care, and telehealth visits; $0 annual and routine labs; and $0 on 100-plus generic medications.

  • More doctors and hospitals: Iowa members have exclusive access to University of Iowa Health Care, MercyOne, and UnityPoint health systems. Members in Kansas City have access to HCA Midwest Health, University of Kansas Health System, and AdventHealth System. Omaha members receive access to CHI Health and Nebraska Methodist Health System.

  • One-on-one guidance: Every member gets access to dedicated Oscar Care Guides and an everyday AI health guide, Oswell4, to help members find care, understand benefits, and receive personalized guidance.

  • Everyday rewards: $50 in Hy-Vee rewards redeemable on groceries, gas, dietitian services, and more.

"Hy-Vee Health with Oscar makes offering competitive benefits easy and affordable for businesses of all sizes,” explained Geoff Bartsh, Senior Vice President of Markets for Oscar Insurance. “As we grow across the Midwest, we’re excited to make healthcare simple, accessible, and affordable for more communities, paired with everyday savings from Hy-Vee.”

“We are proud to expand our partnership with Oscar to bring affordable, high-quality care to more Midwest families through the providers, pharmacies, and stores they know and trust,” said Dr. Jon Van Der Veer, Founder and CEO of Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care.

Employers can enroll their teams at hioscar.com/for-employers, or through their broker. Individuals, families, and employees can sign up through Jan, 15, 2027:

  • Iowa: Visit HealthCare.gov, call 1-833-419-8482, or connect with an insurance agent. Employees receiving tax-free contributions from work, should check with their employers for details.

  • Johnson County, Kansas, and Jackson County, Missouri (Kansas City metro): Visit hioscar.com/get-coverage or connect with an insurance agent.

  • Douglas County, Nebraska (Omaha metro): Visit hioscar.com/get-coverage or connect with an insurance agent.

About Oscar Insurance
Oscar Insurance is one of the largest and fastest-growing health insurers dedicated to the individual market. Oscar serves millions of individuals across the country with innovative products and CHOICE Arrangement solutions (formerly ICHRA) tailored to their life stages, health needs, and budgets. Oscar technology-powered experiences make high-quality care easy to use and feel personal. Oscar is part of Oscar Health, Inc. (). Learn more at HiOscar.com.

About Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care
Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care is a membership-based healthcare organization addressing the evolving needs of today’s patients through accessible, transparent, and relationship-driven care. Operating clinics across five Midwest states, Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care offers healthcare through flexible membership options designed to meet patients where they are in their health journey. The organization is focused on strengthening patient-provider relationships and delivering a more trusted, sustainable healthcare experience.
